title: Matrices: Order, Operations, Transpose and Symmetric Matrices
seo_title: Matrices Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Concept, notation, order, equality, types of matrices, zero and identity matrix, transpose of a matrix, symmetric and skew symmetric matrices; operations on matrices: addition and multiplication and multiplication with a scalar; simple properties of addition, multiplication and scalar multiplication; non-commutativity of multiplication of matrices; invertible matrices (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Matrices worksheet (NCERT Chapter 3): order, aᵢⱼ, equality, addition, scalar multiples, multiplication, AB ≠ BA, transpose, symmetric and skew symmetric matrices. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: AB is defined only when columns of A = rows of B.
key_sub: (AB)′ = B′A′; any square matrix = symmetric part + skew symmetric part.
body_html:
How it works

  • An m × n matrix has m rows and n columns; aij is in row i, column j.
  • Add matrices of the same order entry by entry; kA multiplies every entry by k.
  • AB is defined when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B; multiply rows by columns. In general AB ≠ BA.
  • Transpose A′: rows become columns. Symmetric: A′ = A. Skew symmetric: A′ = −A (diagonal entries 0). A = ½(A + A′) + ½(A − A′).
Example

A = [1 2; 3 4]. Find A².

Row 1 × columns: 1·1 + 2·3 = 7, 1·2 + 2·4 = 10

Row 2: 3·1 + 4·3 = 15, 3·2 + 4·4 = 22

Answer: [7 10; 15 22]

Common mistakes

  • Swapping rows and columns when giving the order.
  • Multiplying matrices entry by entry.
  • Assuming AB = BA.

faq.q: Can a non-square matrix be symmetric?
faq.a: No. A′ = A needs the same order, so the matrix must be square.
